---
title: "Install IQmol and connect to Q-Chem"
subtitle: "Guide 1 · about 15 minutes, once per semester"
---

All calculations in this lab run in **Q-Chem** [@epifanovsky2021], a professional quantum-chemistry program. You won't install Q-Chem on your laptop. Instead you'll use **IQmol** [@iqmol], a free graphical program that builds the molecule, writes the Q-Chem input and **sends the job to a remote server** where Q-Chem actually runs. When the job finishes, IQmol brings the results back.

This is how research computing works: you prepare jobs on your own computer, submit them to a shared machine, and analyze the output when it comes back.

```{=html}
<div class="lab-card" style="margin:1rem 0">
<pre style="margin:0;background:none;font-size:.85rem">
 your laptop                         the Q-Chem server
 ┌─────────────────┐   submit job    ┌──────────────────────┐
 │ IQmol           │ ──────────────▶ │ queue → Q-Chem runs  │
 │ (build, set up, │                 │ (≤ 10 min per job)   │
 │  analyze)       │ ◀────────────── │ output file          │
 └─────────────────┘  results back   └──────────────────────┘
</pre></div>
```

## 1. Install IQmol

1. Go to **[iqmol.org](http://iqmol.org)** and open the **Downloads** page.
2. Download the installer for your operating system (Windows, macOS or Linux).
3. Install it like any other application.
   - **macOS:** if the system says the app "cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified", right-click (or Control-click) IQmol in *Applications*, choose **Open**, then confirm. You only need to do this the first time.
   - **Windows:** if SmartScreen warns you, click **More info → Run anyway**.
4. Launch IQmol. You should see an empty 3D viewer with a toolbar on top.

::: {.callout-note}
The Florida Tech computer labs may already have IQmol installed. Ask your instructor which rooms.
:::

## 2. Connect to the free Q-Chem server

IQmol ships with access to a **free Q-Chem server** for teaching and small calculations.

1. Open any molecule (for example, download one `.xyz` file from [Experiment 1](../experiments/ex01-basis-sets.qmd) and use **File → Open**).
2. Open the Q-Chem setup window (**Calculation → Q-Chem Setup**, or the Q-Chem button on the toolbar).
3. In the **Server** menu at the bottom of the window, select the default free Q-Chem server.
4. The first time, IQmol may ask you to register or accept the server's terms. Follow the prompts and use your Florida Tech e-mail.

::: {.callout-important}
## The 10-minute rule
Jobs on the free server are stopped after **10 minutes** of run time. Everything in Experiments 1–9 is designed to fit, and every experiment page flags the jobs that might be close to the limit. If a job is killed, it is almost always because of a typo in the basis set or method (for example, a much larger basis than intended). See [Working on a shared machine](shared-machines.qmd).
:::

## 3. Check that everything works

Run the test job in the [first-job guide](first-job.qmd): one HCl molecule with HF/def2-SVP. It should finish in a few seconds. If it does, you are ready for the experiments.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | What to try |
|---|---|
| IQmol won't start on macOS | Right-click → **Open** (see above). On Apple-silicon Macs, make sure you downloaded the current version. |
| The server list is empty | Check your internet connection and any firewall or VPN. On campus Wi-Fi it should work out of the box. |
| A job stays "queued" for a long time | The server is shared; at busy times (the night before a deadline!) jobs wait. Submit early. |
| The job fails immediately | Open the output file and read the last lines; there is usually a clear error message. Common culprits: wrong charge or multiplicity, or a misspelled basis set. |
